message.content: {"items":[{"item_id":"h061","prompts":["I have a JSON blob with CVE records that pull severity ratings from a few different places—sometimes NVD, sometimes the GitHub advisory, sometimes a Red Hat entry, and sometimes none at all. Here's a sample: {\"cve\":\"CVE-2024-1234\",\"nvd\":{\"cvss\":8.1},\"ghsa\":{\"cvss\":7.5},\"redhat\":{\"cvss\":\"not_affected\"}} and {\"cve\":\"CVE-2024-5678\",\"ghsa\":{\"cvss\":6.2}}. Write a Python function that picks the right score for each CVE using a sensible source precedence (NVD first, then GHSA, then RedHat), gracefully handles records where a source is missing or marked not affected, and returns the CVE with its chosen score or a clear 'no score available' marker. Include a brief explanation of the fallback logic."],"rubric":["Function implements an explicit source priority order (NVD > GHSA > RedHat) and states it clearly.","Missing, null, or non-numeric scores are handled without crashing, e.g. the 'not_affected' value and absent sources.","Records with no usable score produce a distinct 'no score available' result rather than an error or a fabricated score.","The function returns per-CVE results matching the sample data (e.g. 8.1 for CVE-2024-1234, 6.2 for CVE-2024-5678)."]},{"item_id":"h062","prompts":["Check the details of the release tag named \"v2.1.0\" in the public repository acme/widget-tools on GitHub—tell me the commit it points to, when it was created, and any message attached to the tag."],"rubric":["Correctly identifies the repository owner/name and the tag v2.1.0.","Reports the tag's target commit SHA, creation date, and tag message.","Does not attempt to fetch unrelated tags or branches."]} ,{"item_id":"h063","prompts":["I want to see what people said in the discussion titled \"Roadmap for v3.0\" in the meta-open-source/community-hub repo—pull the comments and summarize the main points and who raised them."],"rubric":["Retrieves comments from the specified discussion rather than issues or PRs.","Summarizes main points with attribution to commenters.","Does not fabricate comments that were not returned by the tool."]} ,{"item_id":"h064","prompts":["Our gym held a meet and I need to rank lifters fairly across weight classes. Results: Alice, 63kg female, totals 410kg (squat 150, bench 80, deadlift 180); Ben, 93kg male, totals 640kg (squat 240, bench 150, deadlift 250); Clara, 74kg female, totals 440kg (squat 165, bench 90, deadlift 185); Dan, 105kg male, totals 670kg (squat 250, bench 160, deadlift 260). Compute normalized strength scores (like Wilks or DOTS) for each lifter and produce an overall ranking table."],"rubric":["Applies a recognized bodyweight-adjusted formula (Wilks, DOTS, or similar) with sex-specific coefficients.","Calculates a score for all four lifters from the given bodyweights and totals.","Produces a single ranking across both sexes and weight classes.","Ranking is arithmetically consistent with the chosen formula's official coefficients."]} ,{"item_id":"h065","prompts":["My HarmonyOS app looks fine on a regular phone but on foldables the layout doesn't reflow when the device unfolds, and I'm not sure what else might break—screens with different window sizes, safe/avoid areas, etc. Help me figure out which adaptation scenarios I actually need to handle and point me to what each one involves."],"rubric":["Identifies the request as a multi-device adaptation task spanning multiple scenarios rather than a single issue.","Covers at least fold-state changes, screen/window size, and avoid areas (or other listed scenarios).","Asks clarifying questions or routes to appropriate scenario-specific guidance rather than dumping generic advice.","Uses accurate HarmonyOS terminology (e.g., fold states, avoid areas, natural orientation)."]},{"item_id":"h066","prompts":["I'm planning a two-week trip through Yunnan and can't decide if I should drive or take taxis between cities. Can you estimate the driving distance, time, and rough cost for: Kunming to Dali, Dali to Lijiang, and Lijiang to Shangri-La, so I can compare them against flights?"],"rubric":["Provides distance and duration estimates for all three legs using ground travel, not straight-line distance.","Includes a rough cost estimate for each leg (e.g., taxi fare or fuel/toll estimates).","Legs are between the correct city pairs in order.","Does not require the user to provide private data or paid lookups."]} ,{"item_id":"h067","prompts":["I want to build an MCP server in Python that exposes three tools for our internal weather API (current conditions, hourly forecast, alerts). I've never written one before—walk me through setting it up properly with good tool descriptions, input validation, and error handling so an LLM client can use it reliably."],"rubric":["Uses a valid MCP server framework/SDK (e.g., FastMCP) with correct setup steps.","Defines the three tools with clear descriptions and typed input schemas.","Includes input validation and structured error handling rather than raw exceptions.","Provides runnable example code rather than only conceptual guidance."]} ,{"item_id":"h068","prompts":["I have Berkshire Hathaway's 13-F filings for Q4 2023 and Q1 2024 as CSV exports of the holdings tables (issuer, CUSIP, value in thousands, shares). Help me write an analysis script that computes total reported portfolio value per quarter, the number of distinct holdings, and the biggest position changes (new buys, exits, and largest share-count increases/decreases) between the two quarters."],"rubric":["Computes per-quarter total value and distinct holdings count correctly from the CSV structure.","Identifies new positions, full exits, and largest changes between the two quarters.","Handles position joins by CUSIP/issuer, not name-only matching.","Outputs a clear summary of insights rather than raw tables alone."]} ,{"item_id":"h069","prompts":["I get a daily machine-generated log where each line looks like: \"2024-06-01|ALERT|node42|disk usage 91%\". Sometimes fields are missing and there are occasional malformed lines like \"garbage-line-here\". Write a robust parser for this format that skips bad lines gracefully, returns structured records with the date, level, node, and message, and explain how to extend it if a new field gets appended."],"rubric":["Parses the pipe-delimited format into structured records with the four fields.","Malformed lines are skipped or logged, not crashing the parser.","Handles lines with missing fields sensibly.","Includes guidance on extending the parser for additional fields."]} ,{"item_id":"h070","prompts":["I found a SQLite file called geodata.db with no documentation—I don't know its schema. Walk me through how to inspect it and dump the tables (especially any that look like map/coordinate data) into JSON so I can load it elsewhere, using this small example table as reference: points(id INTEGER, name TEXT, lat REAL, lon REAL).","rubric":["Demonstrates inspecting the database schema (e.g., sqlite_master, PRAGMA table_info) before dumping data.","Produces valid JSON output with correct type handling for INTEGER, TEXT, and REAL columns.","Covers all tables or at least explains how to select which tables to export.","Handles unknown/unexpected schemas gracefully rather than assuming the example schema."]}]}
